the engineered Ntr regulon controls the expression of the two key enzymes in the lycopene biosynthetic pathway in response to flux changes.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of using a global regulatory system in Escherichiae coli to control the production of a foreign metabolite, lycopene, by sensing the intracellular metabolic state.
we have engineered a metabolic control system that can be applied to improve metabolite production and that this system is based on the Ntr regulons in E. coli.

the design and engineering of a regulatory circuit to achieve optimal metabolic flux and to reduce the negative impact of uncontrolled metabolic pathways.
engineering a new type of gene regulatory system to control gene expression and improve the performance of metabolic engineering.
improving the efficiency of metabolic engineering by engineering the metabolic controls.

we have developed and demonstrated an approach to engineer metabolic control to improve the production of metabolite in engineered cells.
we have developed a new strategy to engineer the metabolic control circuit to achieve a more optimal and efficient metabolic engineering.
the engineered regulatory circuit can control gene expression in the presence of a metabolic flux imbalance and improve the overall productivity of the engineered metabolic pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully demonstrated the second stage effort for metabolic engineering by designing and implementing a regulatory circuit to tightly control metabolic fluxes in response to intrellular metabolic states.
the engineered regulatory system can be used to control metabolic flux and improve metabolite production in engineered metabolic pathways.
we have demonstrated that the metabolic engineering of a regulatory circuit to achieve metabolic control can be an effective strategy for enhancing metabolite production.

the metabolic control of gene expression is a powerful tool to engineer the metabolic pathway.
the metabolic control can be engineered to improve the production of foreign metabolites in the cell.

metabolic engineering is not only a matter of amplifying enzymes and deregulating controls, but also a matter of designing and engineering metabolic controls to achieve optimal metabolic balance and productivity.
